name: Hippopotamus
headline: length
subtitle: Common (river) hippopotamus
description: The common hippopotamus is a huge, barrel-bodied African mammal that spends most of the day wallowing in shallow water and comes ashore at night to graze. San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance gives adults a length of 3.3 to 5 m and a shoulder height of up to 1.6 m. Males are much heavier than females, weighing from about 1,600 kg to as much as 4,500 kg.

measures.label: Length
measures.note: Adult length as listed by San Diego Zoo (10.8 to 16.5 ft); the source does not say whether the tail is included

measures.label: Height at shoulder
measures.note: Up to 5.2 ft (1.6 m) at the shoulder

facts.text: A hippo's eyes, ears and nostrils sit on top of its head, so it can see, hear and breathe while almost fully submerged.
Hippos can hold their breath for five minutes or longer and can even sleep underwater, surfacing to breathe by reflex without waking.
Despite their bulk, hippos eat only about 40 kg (88 lb) of food a night, around 1 to 1.5 percent of their body weight.
Some hippo calls have been measured at 115 decibels.

caveats: No Smithsonian National Zoo page for the common hippopotamus was found, so all figures come from San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance (single source).
The source gives a single 'Length' without saying whether the tail is included.
